comparison: Perfect alignment on core mechanism claims (C4-C6, C29, C69-C70). Both evaluations find the heterogeneous plasticity mechanism for speed control well-supported and novel. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation via simulations and theory, while peer reviewers emphasize novelty as an alternative to existing mechanisms.

Perfect alignment on spiking network implementation (C67-C68, C73). Both evaluations support the extension to biologically plausible spiking networks. OpenEval highlights quantitative biological plausibility (1mV biases), while peer reviewers include this in their overall assessment of convincing characterization.

Perfect alignment on experimental predictions (C91-C97). Both evaluations accept the predictions as logical consequences of the model. OpenEval explicitly notes they are untested speculations, while peer reviewers implicitly accept them as valuable future directions without challenge.

Strong alignment on uniform heterogeneity results (C31, C61, C63). Both find the robustness demonstration convincing. OpenEval also addresses C64 (persistent activity explanation), which peer reviewers include in their evaluation, showing complete agreement on this extension.

Strong alignment on learning mechanism (C65-C66, C72). Both evaluations support the perturbation-based learning rule. OpenEval notes that generalization would benefit from more explicit demonstration, while peer reviewers accept it as part of the model's advantages without raising concerns.

Strong alignment on preparatory-to-execution transitions (C7, C30, C51-C54, C71). Both evaluations support this capability. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of temporal dynamics, while peer reviewers treat it as a key feature within their overall assessment of convincing characterization. Peer review also includes C48-C50 from persistent activity claims.

Strong alignment on speed control characterization (C38-C42, C44-C45). Both evaluations find the quantitative analysis convincing. OpenEval emphasizes phase diagrams and noise robustness, while peer reviewers include these findings (plus C32-C34, C47) in their thorough analysis assessment without specific concerns.

Alignment on comparison with prior work (C85-C86). Both evaluations affirm the model as a novel alternative. OpenEval provides detailed comparison with Murray/Escola and Wang et al., while peer reviewers emphasize the novelty. Peer review also addresses C87-C88 on learning requirements.

Partial disagreement on biological plausibility (C82-C84). OpenEval finds the theoretical justification appropriate and acknowledges experimental gaps honestly. Peer reviewers rate this as UNCERTAIN, noting biological plausibility 'remains an open question' and is left for future work. Peer review also addresses C74, C80-C81 on STDP diversity and functional roles.

Overlap on STDP diversity discussion (C74, C80). OpenEval finds the review of experimental findings appropriate and notes the functional role is speculative. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about biological plausibility mapping. Both acknowledge limitations but OpenEval is more accepting of the discussion as sufficient.

Partial overlap on baseline speed behavior (C32-C34). OpenEval specifically evaluates the linear dependence and 2× slowdown finding. Peer reviewers include these claims in their broader assessment of convincing quantitative characterization without specific focus.

Partial overlap on persistent activity and stopping (C48-C50). OpenEval focuses on phase diagrams and transition to stopped retrieval. Peer reviewers include these claims alongside preparatory-execution transitions in their overall positive assessment.

Minimal overlap on persistent activity requirement (C64). OpenEval explains the mechanistic requirement for finite fraction of symmetric neurons. Peer reviewers include this in their robustness assessment without detailed comment.

Minimal overlap on motor cortex comparison (C58). OpenEval evaluates the qualitative comparison to experimental observations as appropriate. Peer reviewers include C55-C58 in their acceptance of network dynamics characterization without specific focus on experimental comparison.

OpenEval evaluates background/context claims (C1-C3) establishing prior research state and limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers focus on novel contributions rather than background accuracy.

OpenEval evaluates discussion of gating mechanisms (C100-C104) as appropriately speculative with good citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not specifically address gating mechanism discussion.

OpenEval evaluates characterization of prior work and gap identification (C14-C20) as accurate and well-motivated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers focus on novel contributions rather than literature review accuracy.

OpenEval evaluates comparison with recent alternative models (C89-C90, C105-C107) as clear and appropriate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer R8 addresses related comparison claims C85-C88.

OpenEval evaluates theoretical context on optimal connectivity (C109-C111) as appropriate and relevant. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not specifically address theoretical background claims.

OpenEval evaluates model design choice justification (C43) regarding negative inputs as reasonable. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not specifically address this methodological choice.

OpenEval evaluates acknowledgment of learning limitation (C108) as honest and appropriate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers address learning biological plausibility more broadly in R9.
